items.requirement: Non-finite numeric inputs (Infinity, -Infinity) supplied in request bodies are rejected with a 400 error rather than silently producing a null result in a 200 response.
items.rationale: JSON.parse('1e400') yields Infinity, a valid JSON number literal; without an explicit finiteness check the handler would compute a non-finite result and JSON.stringify would silently serialize it as null, giving a misleading 200 response.
items.threshold: Any request to /calculate, /memory/add, or /memory/subtract containing a non-finite numeric operand always returns HTTP 400 with the documented error shape.
items.measurement: Manual verification via real HTTP requests to each affected endpoint with Infinity-valued inputs.

items.requirement: N/A — no special latency or throughput targets.
items.rationale: Sample / evaluation workload only; the added Number.isFinite() check has negligible cost.

items.rationale: The change is confined to the HTTP request-validation layer and must not alter behavior for valid finite-input requests.
items.threshold: All 21 pre-existing Vitest tests pass after the change.
items.measurement: npm test in examples/arithmetic-api — 3 test files, 21 tests.
